config.title: useFetch

intro.title: useFetch
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable `useFetch` custom composition function in Vue.js to fetch and display data from an external API. You will learn the core concept of Vue's Composition API, which allows you to encapsulate and reuse reactive logic across components. The main technologies involved are Vue's `ref` for reactive state, the `fetch` API for HTTP requests, and lifecycle hooks to trigger data fetching. By the end, you'll have a custom hook that manages loading states, errors, and data, making your components cleaner and more maintainable.
intro.usecase: The useFetch pattern is essential for any Vue application that displays dynamic data from APIs. You'll use it to populate dashboards with live metrics, load product catalogs in e-commerce sites, and fetch user profiles in social platforms. This pattern handles loading states, errors, and data updates cleanly, making it fundamental for building responsive, data-driven interfaces like admin panels, news feeds, or real-time analytics displays.

objectives: Implement the useFetch composable to fetch data from an API endpoint
Configure the useFetch composable with options like immediate execution and response type
Initialize reactive state variables to store fetched data, loading status, and error messages
Manipulate the fetched data by transforming or filtering the response before display
Bind the loading and error states to conditional UI elements in your template
Control when the fetch executes by triggering it based on user interactions or component lifecycle
Integrate the useFetch composable into a Vue component to display dynamic data

steps.title: Import ref and onMounted from Vue
steps.instruction: Import ref and onMounted from 'vue' at the top of your file.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the composition API functions you'll need for reactive state and lifecycle hooks.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing Vue composition API functions
import { ref, onMounted } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have access to ref for reactive state and onMounted for lifecycle hooks in your Vue component.
successCriteria: ref and onMounted are imported from 'vue'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both ref and onMounted from 'vue'.

steps.title: Create the useFetch composable function
steps.instruction: Create a function named useFetch that takes a URL parameter. The function should be defined as a composable that can be used in Vue components.
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts a URL parameter. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.seedCode:
// Import ref and onMounted from 'vue'

// Create the useFetch composable function
steps.expectedOutcome: A useFetch function is defined that accepts a URL parameter, ready to be implemented in subsequent steps.
successCriteria: The useFetch function is defined with a URL parameter
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've defined a function named useFetch that accepts a URL parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function definition is missing or incorrect. Create a function named useFetch that takes a URL parameter.

steps.title: Initialize reactive state variables
steps.instruction: Inside the useFetch function, create three ref variables: one named 'data' initialized to null, one named 'loading' initialized to false, and one named 'error' initialized to null.
steps.hint: Use the ref function you imported to create reactive references. Each call to ref returns a reactive reference that holds the value you pass as the initial argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useFetch function will have three reactive state variables ready to track API data, loading status, and potential errors.
successCriteria: Three ref variables are created inside useFetch: data (null), loading (false), and error (null).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created some state variables, but make sure you have all three: data, loading, and error, each initialized with the correct default values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useFetch function doesn't contain the required reactive state variables. Create three ref variables: data (null), loading (false), and error (null).

steps.title: Define the fetchData function
steps.instruction: Inside the useFetch function, define an async function named fetchData that will handle the API call.
steps.hint: Use the async keyword before function to make it asynchronous. You can define it as a regular function or arrow function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useFetch function now contains an async fetchData function definition.
successCriteria: An async function named fetchData is defined inside the useFetch function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've defined an async function named fetchData inside useFetch.
steps.feedbackWrong: The fetchData function isn't defined correctly. Check that it's an async function inside useFetch.

steps.title: Implement error handling in fetchData
steps.instruction: Inside the fetchData function, wrap the fetch call in a try-catch block to handle errors and update the error state variable.
steps.hint: Use try { ... } catch (error) { ... } around your fetch logic. In the catch block, set the error state variable to the error message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The fetchData function should include a try-catch block to gracefully handle API errors and update the error state.
successCriteria: The fetchData function contains a try-catch block that catches errors and updates the error state variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to wrap the fetch call in a try-catch block and update the error state in the catch block.
steps.feedbackWrong: The fetchData function doesn't have proper error handling. Add a try-catch block to handle errors.

steps.title: Call fetchData on component mount
steps.instruction: Inside the useFetch function, call the fetchData function when the component mounts using the onMounted lifecycle hook.
steps.hint: Use onMounted() and pass fetchData as the callback function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The fetchData function will be automatically called when any component using useFetch is mounted.
successCriteria: onMounted is called with fetchData as the callback inside the useFetch function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling onMounted() and passing fetchData as the callback inside the useFetch function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The fetchData function needs to be called automatically when the component mounts using onMounted.

steps.title: Return the reactive state from useFetch
steps.instruction: Inside the useFetch function, return an object containing the data, loading, error, and fetchData variables so they can be accessed by components that use this composable.
steps.hint: Use the return statement at the end of your useFetch function. The object should include all the reactive state variables you initialized earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useFetch function now returns an object containing data, loading, error, and fetchData, making these available to any component that calls useFetch().
successCriteria: The useFetch function returns an object with data, loading, error, and fetchData properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're returning an object with all four properties: data, loading, error, and fetchData. Check that you're using the correct variable names you initialized earlier.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useFetch function needs to return an object containing the reactive state variables. Look at the analogous example to see how to structure the return statement.

steps.title: Create the main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named 'App' with a setup function that will use the useFetch composable.
steps.hint: Define a new component function that returns a template. Inside, you'll call useFetch in the next step.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have an App component ready to use the useFetch composable in its setup.
successCriteria: The App component is defined as a function with a setup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you define a function named 'App'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined yet. Create a function named 'App'.

steps.title: Use the useFetch composable in the component
steps.instruction: Inside your component's setup function, call the useFetch composable with a sample API URL (like 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/todos/1') and destructure the returned values into data, error, and loading variables.
steps.hint: Call useFetch() with a URL string as an argument, then destructure the object it returns using curly braces.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: calling a composable and destructuring
const { result, isLoading } = useApi('https://api.example.com/data');
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now calls useFetch with a URL and destructures its return values, making them available for use in the template.
successCriteria: useFetch is called with a URL string inside setup(), and its return values are destructured into data, error, and loading.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling useFetch() with a URL argument and destructuring all three values (data, error, loading).
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't match the required action. Inside setup(), call useFetch('your-url') and destructure the returned object.

steps.title: Display the fetched data and states in the template
steps.instruction: In your component's template section, add conditional rendering to display loading text when loading is true, an error message when error exists, and the fetched data when available.
steps.hint: Use Vue's template syntax with v-if directives to conditionally render different content based on the state values returned from useFetch.

steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display 'Loading...' while fetching, show an error message if the fetch fails, and display the fetched data when successful.
successCriteria: The template contains v-if directives that conditionally render loading text, error messages, and fetched data based on the reactive state values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some conditional rendering, but make sure you're handling all three states (loading, error, and data) with appropriate v-if directives.
